aboutH2: Orca Lelum: Indigenous Youth Wellness in Lantzville
intro: Orca Lelum is an Indigenous-led youth wellness centre in Lantzville, a few minutes north of Nanaimo. It works with Indigenous youth aged 12 to 18 from anywhere in British Columbia who are dealing with substance use and mental health challenges. The centre calls itself one of only two Indigenous youth wellness centres in BC, and its website says it is accepting intake applications now.

The care starts from culture. Orca Lelum describes its model as Indigenous healing practices woven together with clinical supports, guided by Snuw'uyulh (Coast Salish teachings) and the principle of Nutsamaat Shqwaluwun, working together with one heart and one mind. The centre puts it plainly: clinical services support the care, and culture leads the healing.

pillars.title: A Wellness Centre on Snaw-Naw-As Lands
pillars.body: Orca Lelum is on Capilano Road in Lantzville, on the ancestral lands of Snaw-Naw-As First Nation, between Nanaimo and Parksville. Youth live on site for the whole program. The days use the land and water around the centre: hiking, mountain biking, swimming, fishing and time in nature sit alongside counselling and ceremony. Inside there are spaces for art and music, and the building is wheelchair accessible.

pillars.title: Three Months of Continued Connection
pillars.body: Planning for home is part of the live-in program. Youth learn relapse prevention tools, build a wellness plan and set goals for life after Orca Lelum, and the team makes referrals to resources in their own community. Once they leave, youth can stay connected with the Orca Lelum team for up to 3 months. Family wellness workers and aftercare support workers are both part of the staff.

pillars.title: Nine Nations and a Team of More Than 50
pillars.body: The Orca Lelum Wellness Society is governed by a Board of Directors representing nine Coast Salish member Nations: Halalt, Lyackson, Malahat, Penelakut, Qualicum, Snaw-Naw-As, Snuneymuxw, Stz'uminus and Ts'uubaa-asatx. Day to day, more than 50 staff do the work, including regulated health professionals, a holistic trauma advisor, counsellors, social workers, cultural coordinators, youth support workers and youth advocates. Elders and Knowledge Keepers guide the cultural teachings.

overview: The Live-In Wellness Program has been running since 2024. It is voluntary and structured, and it is meant for Indigenous youth with mild substance use and mental health challenges. Each young person works with the Care Team on an individual care plan. Health care, mental health support, nutrition and healthy meals are part of daily life, and a kinesiologist and occupational therapists help youth stay active.
serviceCaption: 12 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Healing is framed through the Longhouse and its four posts, which stand for heart, mind, body and spirit. Looking at all four helps youth and staff see where life is out of balance and build a wellness plan to restore it. Cultural activities include weaving, painting, storytelling, drumming and singing, an introduction to traditional medicines and plants, and ceremonies such as blanket ceremonies, cedar brushings and spirit baths. The centre also lists a Withdrawal Management Program for 7 to 14 day stays as coming soon, at a new purpose-built centre. It is not open yet.

location.heading: Orca Lelum in Lantzville, British Columbia
location.intro: Orca Lelum is at 699 Capilano Road in Lantzville, on central Vancouver Island, about 15 minutes north of Nanaimo and the Departure Bay ferry terminal. From Vancouver, plan on roughly 2.5 to 3 hours including the Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay ferry; Victoria is about 1 hour 45 minutes south, Parksville about 20 minutes north and Duncan in the Cowichan Valley about an hour away.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.a: Orca Lelum is for Indigenous youth aged 12 to 18 who live in British Columbia and have a valid BC Medical Services Card. Programming is co-ed and open to 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, and the facility is wheelchair accessible. Youth need parental or guardian consent, should be able to handle daily self-care and live with others, and are expected to take part in all parts of the program, including ceremony.

faqs.q: What kind of program does Orca Lelum offer?
faqs.a: Orca Lelum runs a voluntary Live-In Wellness Program where youth stay on site for 9 to 10 weeks. It is designed for youth with mild substance use and mental health challenges. The program combines Coast Salish cultural teachings and ceremony with clinical supports such as one-to-one counselling, group circles, equine therapy and trauma care.
Youth live at Orca Lelum for 9 to 10 weeks. After the live-in program, the team stays in touch for up to 3 months to help with relapse prevention, wellness goals and referrals to community resources.

Not yet. The centre's website lists a Withdrawal Management Program as coming soon, for youth with moderate substance use challenges, with 7 to 14 day stays at a new purpose-built Withdrawal Management Centre. Until it opens, ask the intake team where a youth who needs detox should go first.

faqs.q: How do I apply or make a referral?
faqs.a: Email the Intake Team at intake@orcalelum.ca with your name and phone number, and say whether you are referring yourself or contacting them for someone else. Youth can fill in the intake package on their own or with a referring worker. A doctor or nurse practitioner must complete a pre-admission medical assessment.

faqs.q: How much does Orca Lelum cost?
faqs.a: Orca Lelum does not publish a fee on its website. The BC government announced more than $7 million in provincial funding for the centre in April 2024, with another $1 million from Island Health, and it partners with the First Nations Health Authority. Ask the intake team about any costs, including travel.

The Orca Lelum Wellness Society runs the centre. It is an Indigenous-led organization governed by a Board of Directors representing nine Coast Salish member Nations: Halalt, Lyackson, Malahat, Penelakut, Qualicum, Snaw-Naw-As, Snuneymuxw, Stz'uminus and Ts'uubaa-asatx.

faqs.q: Who might not be a fit for Orca Lelum?
faqs.a: Orca Lelum cannot admit youth with unstable medical or psychiatric conditions, youth at imminent risk of suicide, or youth who need continuous one-to-one support or hospital-level care. Youth with psychiatric conditions, eating disorders, self-injury, aggressive behaviour, fire-setting or sex-related legal concerns are not ruled out, but the team will have extra conversations first to see whether it can meet their needs.

faqs.q: Where is Orca Lelum and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Orca Lelum is at 699 Capilano Road in Lantzville, about 15 minutes north of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. From Vancouver, plan on roughly 2.5 to 3 hours with the BC Ferries crossing from Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay in Nanaimo. From Victoria it is about 1 hour 45 minutes north on Highway 1.

faqs.q: What happens after the live-in program?
faqs.a: Before youth leave, they make a wellness plan and set goals for life after the program, and they learn tools to prevent relapse. The Orca Lelum team stays connected for up to 3 months afterward and helps with referrals to community resources. Family wellness work is part of the program too.
